title: How to Mix Vintage and Modern Furniture
summary: Discover the art of mixing vintage and modern furniture to create a curated, balanced space that looks timeless and feels collected.
body_markdown:
[Wall Street Residence by Casa Angulo. Photo by Jenna Saraco](https://www.1stdibs.com/photo/contemporary-living-room-new-york-ny/11183982/)


Mixing modern and vintage furniture works beautifully when it’s done well. Combining furniture from different eras makes a home feel layered, personal and cohesive. Here’s how to do it.


---


## Start with Balance: The 70/30 Rule


[Southeastern Designer Showhouse 2024 by Atelier Davis. Photo by Elliot Fuerniss](https://www.1stdibs.com/project/southeastern-designer-showhouse-2024-atlanta-ga/352502/)


It all starts with the right balance. Most rooms lean one way and typically showcase mostly modern pieces with vintage accents. However, the reverse can work well in some rooms.


That’s the idea behind the 70/30 rule, although it is more of a guideline: Rooms tend to look amazing when 70 percent of the decor is in a dominant style (like clean-lined contemporary) with 30 percent in an accent style (like weathered vintage). This mix can create visual depth.


Start with one vintage piece, like a chair or table, and build outward. Start browsing a reputable[vintage furniture collection](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/) to find your perfect piece.


---


## **Tie It Together with Color and Finish**


[Light-Green Italian Birch Sideboard with 4 Grisinato Glass Doors, 2024](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/storage-case-pieces/credenzas/light-green-italian-birch-sideboard-4-grisinato-glass-doors-available/id-f_40833312/)


To make a mix look and feel intentional, repeat a particular color (black) or material (walnut, brass) at least three times across different heights and functions in the room.


For example, if you have a vintage walnut coffee table, tie it into a new walnut-framed armchair, and then add accents like a contemporary wood picture frame or wooden bowl.


Vintage wood tones pair well with modern neutrals, adding character and depth without clashing. For example, an antique table could anchor your dining room, while minimalist chairs soften the traditional look.


---


## **Match Scale and Silhouette**


[Classic Colonial in Harding, New Jersey, by J. Patryce Design. Photo by Tim Lenz](https://www.1stdibs.com/photo/british-colonial-modern-transitional-living-room-harding-township-nj/11167452/)


When you mix antique, vintage and modern furniture, pay close attention to each piece’s scale and silhouette. Matching pieces based on these elements makes a room feel cohesive instead of chaotic. In adding[vintage seating](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/) to a contemporary decor, say, choose pieces that echo the clean lines or geometric profiles of nearby contemporary ones.


A good example would be pairing a low-profile mid-century modern credenza with a minimalist low-backed contemporary sofa. A bad example would be placing an oversize vintage armchair next to a slim contemporary sofa.


And remember, some highly detailed vintage pieces need negative space around them to prevent visual clutter. When your eye has a chance to rest and appreciate the craftsmanship, that vintage piece will make a statement.


---


## **Mix Textures and Materials**


[Pair of](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/lounge-chairs/french-art-deco-pair-of-lounge-chairs-curved-armests/id-f_51834132/)[French Art Deco Lounge Chairs with Curved Armrests, 1930s](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/seating/lounge-chairs/french-art-deco-pair-of-lounge-chairs-curved-armests/id-f_51834132/)


Mixing older, tactile materials with sleek, hard surfaces allows you to combine pieces with contrasting forms. Vintage leather juxtaposed with modern chrome and reclaimed wood juxtaposed with glass are classic examples. The contrast between the materials adds depth as your eye processes different layers of sensory information.


One of the quickest ways to unify a design is to lay[vintage rugs and carpets](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/rugs-carpets/) that bridge the gap between old and new.


---


## **Room-by-Room Ideas**


[Mid-Century Midwestern Home by Susan Yely](https://www.1stdibs.com/introspective-magazine/susan-yeley-mid-century-modern-home/)


Whether you are looking at[vintage dining tables](https://www.1stdibs.com/furniture/tables/dining-room-tables/) or a modern ottoman, here are some examples of how to mix furniture from different periods, room by room.


- Living room: Pair a vintage mid-century modern credenza with a low-profile, clean-lined modern linen sectional sofa.


- Dining room: Partner vintage mid-century bentwood dining chairs with a contemporary concrete dining table.


- Bedroom: Place an antique wood nightstand next to a modern platform bed fitted with minimalist linen bedding.


- Entryway: Hang a vintage Victorian wall mirror above a floating console shelf.


---


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can you mix vintage and modern furniture?**


Yes, you can mix vintage and modern furniture, tying the pieces together with balance, color, scale and texture.


### **How do you keep a mixed room from looking cluttered?**


To keep a mixed room from looking cluttered, stick with a limited palette, incorporate negative space and design around a single focal piece.


### **What is a good ratio of vintage to modern?**


For a balanced blend, go with 70 percent modern and 30 perent vintage. This recommendation is a guideline, not a rule, as some people prefer a more historic or classic approach, with 40 percent modern and 60 percent vintage. The latter is ideal for older homes, eclectic collectors and character-rich spaces.


### **Which vintage pieces pair best with modern interiors?**


You have many options, ranging from desks and nightstands to statement mirrors and rugs. Chairs, case pieces and lighting are the easiest entry points, because they are standalone sculptural elements that contrast beautifully against clean, minimalist backdrops.


### **Do vintage and modern pieces have to match?**


No, vintage and modern pieces do not have to match. Interior designers actually discourage that in order to create a collected, layered and dynamic decor. The key is to choose pieces that relate through color, scale or material.


### **Is it expensive to insert vintage pieces into a modern home?**


Mixing vintage furniture into your home doesn’t need to be expensive. But prices vary. You don’t need to purchase all the pieces you’ll want at once. Start with one and grow your collection over time.


---


## **Mixing Styles Works When Designed Well**


As you start creating your decor blending antique and modern furniture, repetition — whether of tone, scale or texture — helps tie pieces together, creating a cohesive look.
